turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, Hale, so you have twenty-five minutes. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Start there.
Before we start, I reread Owen's last three essays this morning.
This morning. The zero went in a week ago, so you checked after you'd decided, and you still haven't told me why nobody called me first.
He writes like someone who was read to every night. That was you, wasn't it?
Don't manage me, Hale. Why did nobody call me before that zero went in?
You've raised a genuinely thoughtful kid. I mean that.
Then why are we here? Answer my question or I'm going upstairs.
Which is why I'd hate for this to become a fight between two people who obviously both care about him.
You didn't care enough to pick up the phone before you entered a zero. That's against your own procedure, section 4.2, and I have it printed in my bag. Who decided, and was Owen heard first?
